leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open as this run starts — the balance is positive and nothing is at risk from the lock. What needs watching is that the recommended moves deliberately open one. The Muheim sale lands first and lifts the balance; Ryerson resolves this evening and takes most of that back; Curda, if he wins, resolves tomorrow midday and pushes the balance negative. That deficit would sit open for roughly three days against a four-day lock, which is ample, but it is not optional to clear it: a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the entire matchday. Three clean unwinds exist, any one of which is sufficient — sell either new defender back to the board at exactly market value, or sell Tanaka and Adamu, the two weakest bodies. Spending power is governed by the floor rather than by cash, and both bids together sit well inside it, so affordability is not the constraint; the unwind is.

binding_gap: Defence, and it is created by the sale rather than discovered. With Muheim gone the squad is down to three defenders and the bare eleven, which forces the three-four-three and pulls the weakest attacker into the fielded side. Ryerson closes it tonight; Curda would close it again tomorrow midday if that offer wins. Either one alone is enough to restore a choice of formation, and both landing is comfortable rather than a problem.

sell.reason: Muheim, and only Muheim. He went off after about twenty minutes in the nil-four at Werder on 22 November with a calf problem — his own words were that there is something in the calf, with no contact and no timeline, and Polzin's reaction was that it hurts and that he had been in outstanding form. Kickbase has already set a non-zero status flag against him. HSV host Bayern on Saturday and nothing dated says he will be available. His average is a pre-injury number carried largely by two very big scores, so it flatters him. Sell him back to the board, which pays exactly market value with no spread, and do it before tonight's tick rather than after: his rising flag was set at last night's tick, which was before the injury happened, so the flag cannot know about the calf and tonight's tick is the first one that can price it. That is the one case where the usual rule of selling risers after the tick does not apply. The sale drops the squad to the bare eleven and forces the three-four-three, which is exactly why the replacement matters more than the sale.

buy.reason: Ryerson is the move, and this run changes what he is. Previous runs had him down as a value flip to be bought at market value and sold straight back after the tick; he is now a defender to keep, because he fills the hole the Muheim sale opens. His listing is a plain board row with no manager behind it, priced at market value exactly, with nobody else bidding on it as of this run, and it expires this evening before the tick. His fitness and his place are settled by his own data rather than by news: he started his last matchday, played almost the full match, and scored heavily. The two matchdays before that were short substitute appearances, so the recent-cameo trap does not apply in reverse here — the full start is the most recent fact. Bid one euro over market value, not exactly market value: this ledger has twice lost a board row by a single euro, and the never-raise rule is a flip rule that should not be carried into a defender you actually need. Beyond that one euro, do not chase; the contested tail on rows this size has been measured well into double-digit percentages and paying it would be a separate decision. The Curda offer placed yesterday is still live and should be held exactly where it is — not raised, not pulled. His record is clean, every league appearance this season has been a start and the status flag is zero, but the newest dated item about him is five weeks old, so he is backed by a clean record rather than by current news. Both of these are defenders and both are the binding gap; nothing is being padded into a position already covered. Banks is rejected despite looking like the cheapest way to fill the same gap: a big average on a cheap defender with a non-zero status flag is the trap the market has already priced, and his points total implies only a handful of appearances behind that average.
